Authors: Luka Horvat (outside co-author); Maja Popović (R0906); Radovan Bešlin (outside co-author); Elena Ferreira (outside co-author).
Keywords: federated learning; atrial fibrillation; ECG; wearable; privacy-preserving; domain adaptation.
Training robust atrial fibrillation detectors on data pooled from multiple clinical sites raises significant patient privacy concerns. Federated learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving alternative by training shared model parameters without centralizing raw recordings. This work presents a federated AF detection framework tailored to the heterogeneous signal characteristics encountered when aggregating data from four distinct wearable ECG patch platforms with differing sampling rates, electrode configurations, and noise profiles. A domain-adaptive normalization layer is inserted before each local model head to compensate for device-specific distributional shifts. Communication efficiency is improved through gradient sparsification with a threshold calibrated per round.
